Difficulty Notes: Easy optimization problem with intuitive solution
Question: Assume: 1) no-inter player trading occurs, 2) there are no development cards left to draw, 3) in-hand VP cards count as points, 4) can use the combined Trade/Build phase, 5)For maritime trade, a city on a special harbor grants a 1:1 trade rate for its resource, while a city on a generic harbor grants a 3:2 trade rate for any resource. What is the maximum number of unique harbor locations that the green player can have a settlement/city on by the end of the turn, given the player rolls a 3 in this turn? Return the answer in the following format: [prev_harbors: <number of harbors with the players city/settlements before the turn>, new_harbors: <number of harbors with the players city/settlements after the turn>]
Rationale: According to the given board state in the question, the green player has: 1 city at special harbour, and 3 settlements. The current resource pool of the green player is: [brick: 3, wool: 4, grain: 1, lumber: 3, ore: 3]. The development cards include: 1 road building, 1 year of plenty and 1 knight. Also has 3 knights already placed on the table. The total number of points the green player currently has is: 5 points (2 from city + 3 settlements). Since the player rolls a 3 in this turn, the green player gets: 4 grain resources. Making the new resource pool: [brick: 3, wool: 4, grain: 5, lumber: 3, ore: 3]. In order to get the maximum unique harbors: Use the development card of road building and build 2 roads: (3,2) and 3 farms, extending the longest road (of the green player). Then we have enough resources for building a settlement at that generic harbor (3 of farm). There is also one more generic port where one more settlement can be built: (9 of forests). This way 2 settlements can be build on 2 generic harbors making the total number of unique harbors by the end of this turn to be: 3.
